Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-109516 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.0. The `/wp-json/woo-telegram/v1/main/` REST endpoint is registered with `permission_callback => '__return_true'` and performs no Telegram webhook signature verification, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to POST a forged bot update with a `message.chat.id` set to any WordPress login name; `bftow_get_user_system_id()` resolves this attacker-supplied value to the targeted account via `get_user_by('login', $tgId)` with no ownership proof, and writes a login token computed as `md5($_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'] . time())` — both inputs are fully attacker-controlled or bounded within seconds using the response's own `Date` header. The resulting token is redeemable at the unauthenticated, capability-check-free, and nonce-less `?action=bftow_create_order&bftow_token=` endpoint, which calls `wp_set_auth_cookie()` unconditionally via `login_user_by_id`, issuing a persistent authenticated session cookie for the targeted account to the attacker. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any WordPress user, including administrators, given only that user's username.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-287

Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-116576 affectant systeminformation (npm) (score CVSS 7.8).

systeminformation vulnerable to Windows command injection in services() through Unicode quotation marks

This report confirms version 5.33.15 . Other package versions have not been checked.

In lib/processes.js , services() sanitizes the caller's string with sanitizeShellString() and later inserts each resulting name into a Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter command. The Windows branch passes that command to util.powerShell() .

The sanitizer in lib/util.js removes the ASCII double quote, but it does not remove U+201C or U+201D, the left and right curly double quotation marks. It also permits spaces and parentheses when called in its default, non-strict mode. PowerShell accepts the curly marks as string delimiters, so an input can end the filter string and place a command expression in the generated command.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par Unit 42.

Unit 42 explores key peak shopping season retail cyber threats, from ransomware to AI attacks, and shares how to defend operations and customer trust. Unit 42 explores key peak shopping season retail cyber threats, from ransomware to AI attacks, and shares how to defend operations and customer trust.

This blog explores the main cyber threats that retail organizations need to be aware of and prepared to defend against as we approach peak shopping season in 2026. We highlight notable security events that occurred in prior years during this time period. We also examine relevant threats from both an enterprise and guest point of view and provide examples of the evolving trend of autonomous attacks that could impact retailers.

Since 2020, there have been several notable security events disclosed toward the end of peak shopping season. Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Hackers stole passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers for about 2,000 customers.

Japan Airlines said one of its IT providers suffered a data breach that leaked the personal records of more than 90,000 customers, adding to a series of cyberattacks on Japanese firms that has prompted government action in recent days.

The company published a notice on Wednesday saying Amadeus IT Group, the company that runs its flight reservation, ticketing and check-in systems, informed the firm last week that hackers accessed a “portion of customer reservation data” for Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air flights. In total, 92,000 customers were impacted, with hackers accessing names, reservation codes and flight information.

For about 2,000 Japan Airlines customers, the hackers stole passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers.

Japan Airlines said the breach never impacted flight operations and credit card numbers were not compromised.

“We will contact the affected customers individually to provide necessary assistance, including reminders to remain vigilant against phishing emails, fraudulent phone calls, and suspicious websites impersonating the JAL Group,” the company said.

The data breach follows multiple high-profile data breaches impacting Japanese companies over the last two weeks. On Tuesday, an internet service provider owned by Sony Network Communications said more than 2.5 million people had information stolen during a data breach earlier this month.

Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said the incident may be part of a broader campaign targeting both citizens' personal data and government digital infrastructure, according to local media reports.

Moldova is investigating whether foreign state actors were involved in a major cyberattack on its government systems that exposed sensitive personal information and disrupted dozens of public services, the country's prime minister said Wednesday.

Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said the incident may be part of a broader campaign targeting both citizens' personal data and government digital infrastructure, according to local media reports.

"Our country is the target of coordinated and large-scale cyberattacks. We are not talking about an isolated incident," Tofan said, adding that authorities were examining the possible involvement of foreign state actors.

Moldova has not publicly attributed the attack to any country or hacking group.

Tofan's statement came a day after Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency (AGE) disclosed that hackers had exploited vulnerabilities in government services to extract large volumes of personal information between October 19 and 23.

The attackers made approximately 11 million requests to access data through government services. Preliminary findings indicate that information linked to about 750,000 identification numbers was extracted, although not every affected individual had all categories of personal data exposed.

Jérémy Grégoire, l’un de ses animateurs, a annoncé l’incident sur Facebook, exprimant sa colère face à ce qu’il décrit comme plus de dix années de travail anéanties.

Créée en 2016, Liberté FM diffuse ses programmes sur 96,1 MHz dans le Périgord ribéracois . La station couvre l’actualité locale, la culture, le sport et les événements associatifs. Elle réalise également des interviews, des reportages et des émissions disponibles en podcast.

Jérémy Grégoire témoigne de l’émotion suscitée par cette cyberattaque. L’animateur évoque les années d’émissions, de rencontres et de souvenirs accumulés depuis la création de la radio.

Derrière cette station locale se trouve une équipe particulièrement investie. Selon le Club de la presse du Périgord, Liberté FM réunissait en 2024 trois salariés et une trentaine de bénévoles, produisant plus de 50 heures de programmes originaux par semaine .

Ces productions constituent une véritable mémoire du territoire : témoignages d’habitants, interviews de personnalités locales, événements sportifs, initiatives associatives et rencontres culturelles.

La cyberattaque menace donc potentiellement un patrimoine sonore constitué pendant une décennie, dont certaines séquences pourraient être impossibles à enregistrer de nouveau.

Signal de veille — The Record.

A federal appellate court panel said West Virginia's version of Daniel's Law — meant to shield the personal data of police and other officials — is unconstitutional.

A federal appeals court on Tuesday ruled that a West Virginia law meant to shield law enforcement officers and judges from over-exposure of their personal information is unconstitutional.

The 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a lower court’s August 2025 decision nullifying the state’s version of Daniel’s Law, which the opinion said is notably different from similar laws on the books in more than a dozen other states.

The statutes are aimed at keeping disgruntled residents from obtaining officials’ addresses and phone numbers, particularly through data brokers.

The panel of judges found the West Virginia statute unlawfully restricts speech based solely on the topic, message, or subject matter of what is being said — also known as content-based speech — and holds data brokers liable in too many circumstances.

The decision is a significant win for data brokers, which have increasingly been targeted by lawsuits seeking to punish them for business tactics they rely on to operate.

The ruling could influence a court ruling on ongoing Daniel’s Law litigation in New Jersey and impact similar statutes in other states, according to a blog post from the international law firm Clark Hill.

The Austria-based digital privacy advocacy group noyb on Tuesday filed five complaints against a major artificial intelligence company alleging that its practices violate European law by tracking freelance workers’ web activity as they generate AI model training data.

The complaints — filed in France , Italy , the Netherlands and Austria against Scale AI – also allege the firm illegally requires workers’ to submit biometric data.

Noyb’s complaints focused on Scale’s Outlier platform, which is used by tech giants such as Google, Meta and OpenAI. Meta owns nearly half of Scale.

Scale has worked with more than 900,00 people to create the training data. Noyb alleges the platform in some cases records freelancers’ mouse clicks and keystrokes every few seconds and claims the collected information can be used to generate video documenting freelancers’ entire workday.

The data collected by the trackers includes IP addresses, contact details, unique identifiers and “information about the visited page,” noyb said in a press release, and can be used for targeted advertising.

Noyb spokesperson Mickey Manakas said an analysis identified 18 third-party trackers used by Scale to track French freelancers’ data.

The Treasury Department on Wednesday sanctioned Russian and North Korean nationals and companies in the latest round of actions targeting Pyongyang's illicit IT worker campaign.

Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas are accused of helping North Korea launder millions in cryptocurrency payments earned by North Koreans based in Russia working in IT roles at U.S. companies.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said North Korea’s government “continues targeting and exploiting American companies through fraudulent activities conducted by its overseas IT operatives, who weaponize sensitive data and extort businesses for substantial payments.”

Wednesday’s sanctions also include multiple North Koreans, including Kim Hyo Dong and Kim Ki Hyok, a senior Alis employee.

North Korean company First Financial and Technical Development Center was also sanctioned on Wednesday for its alleged role in managing millions of dollars earned by North Koreans based in Russia.

The company has helped IT workers use artificial intelligence as they attempt to get hired at U.S. companies, the Treasury said, and has used sophisticated money laundering methods to conceal the money earned by the workers.

Il y a encore quelques années, la sécurité des données tenait à une question : où sont mes bases ? L'IA en ajoute une seconde. Chaque question posée à ChatGPT, Claude ou Gemini part chez son fournisseur, sur ses serveurs, dans son pays, sous ses lois, avec tout ce qu'on y a collé : un contrat, un tableau client, un CV. Les bases peuvent rester en France. Les questions, elles, voyagent. Yaniv Adjedj, CEO de Reboot Conseil https://reboot-conseil.com/ (cabinet de conseil en IT, IA et cybersécurité) et de Lamalo.ai https://lamalo.ai/fr ((plateforme d'orchestration IA agnostique et souveraine) observe ce basculement : « La souveraineté des données ne se résume plus à leur lieu de stockage. Avec l'IA, les entreprises doivent aussi maîtriser leur circulation, les conditions de leur traitement et les législations qui s'appliquent. Ces enjeux doivent désormais peser autant que la performance dans le choix d'un modèle. » Deux exemples illustratifs : • Le CLOUD Act oblige les entreprises américaines à livrer les données qu'elles contrôlent, même stockées en France.
